subject: red kangaroo
title: One 3,500-Mile Fence Is Changing How Kangaroos Grow Up

scenes.text: Red kangaroos grow up differently depending on which side of one fence they live.
Australia's dingo fence runs about 3,500 miles to keep dingoes from sheep.
Inside it, dingoes are rare, and kangaroos can be about ten times more crowded.
Outside, where dingoes hunt, young kangaroos are heavier with longer feet, and young males have bigger skulls.
One idea: dingoes pick off small kangaroos, so the fast growers survive.
A fence built to protect sheep may be reshaping the kangaroos on the other side.

description:
Red kangaroos on either side of Australia's dingo fence are growing up differently.
The fence runs 5,614 km (about 3,500 miles) to keep dingoes away from sheep. A 2023 study compared red kangaroos at two sites on either side: where dingoes were rare, kangaroos were about ten times denser, while on the dingo side females and young males were heavier with longer feet, and young males had larger skulls. Researchers suggest dingoes may target young, light kangaroos, so fast growth pays off.
What do you think happens if the fence ever comes down?
first_comment: On the dingo-free side there are also far more kangaroos and emus. Should the fence stay?
